text:
maria: heads up — eu-west1 apiserver 503s started around 08:32 UTC, coinciding with a large GPU onboarding batch. kube-dns shows mass cache evictions, QPS spikes to the DNS service. Anyone seeing controller-manager lease or etcd churn? :eyes:

leo: seeing controller-manager lease renewals backlog, controller queue depth up ~3x. apiserver error rate spiked at the same time. attaching a quick snippet of the watch queue metrics:
```
controller_queue_depth{controller="node",region="eu-west1"} 324 -> 987
apiserver_5xx_rate 0.02 -> 0.35
```

ashwin: etcd leader flipped twice in the last 5m, WAL write latencies spiked to ~120ms. suspecting a cascade: DNS cache evictions -> apiserver re-resolves etcd endpoints -> short connection thrash causing leader instability.

sophie: kube-dns pod on eu-west1-1 had OOMKilling GC events earlier, memory pressure looks real. provisioner logs show aggressive retries when k8s api returns 5xx, so that amplifies traffic.

maria: pausing onboarding in eu-west1 now (provisioner freeze). rerouting new GPU requests to us-west. Can someone confirm if rolling apiserver config change (max-conns) helps short term?

leo: short mitigation: increase apiserver --max-requests-inflight and bump apiserver proxy timeout. I can push a canary. /cc @ashwin for ectd-side mitigations.

ashwin: canary for apiserver params rolling to 2 controlplane nodes now. also enabling longer KV cache TTL on the runtime to reduce cold etcd reads. Deploying patch to reduce provisioner retry rate.

deploy-bot: rollout started for apiserver-config v2026.3.1 -> nodes: cp-eu-01, cp-eu-02 (canary)

sophie: noticed provisioner sends bursts of DNS queries when it retries; we should add exponential backoff and jitter to onboarding path. Also consider increasing kube-dns memory cap and tuning GC thresholds.

maria: opening infra-provisioner issue to throttle retries and add jitter: https://internal.redwood/infra/issue/987 (action: on-call to triage).

ashwin: etcd metrics: wal_sync_time spike correlated with snapshot compaction + NVMe IO pressure during GPU attach. leader CPU at 92% for the node that flipped. Long-running reconciles piling up in controller-manager.

leo: roll freeze confirmed reduced 503s from 0.35 -> 0.06 within 3 minutes. watch latency still ~12-18s higher than baseline. We should still follow through with DNS and provisioner fixes.

sophie: action items summarized: 1) throttle provisioner retries + jitter, 2) bump kube-dns memory / GC thresholds, 3) canary apiserver config expanded short-term, 4) investigate NVMe snapshot IO overlap with GPU attach, 5) post-incident followup and runbook updates.

maria: filing in incidents channel and will collect logs for a postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
